new.title: Climb to the towers of Orléans Cathedral
new.desc: The Gothic Cathédrale Sainte-Croix was built from the late 13th century and only completed in 1829. It is a minor basilica and the seat of the diocese of Orléans, dominating Rue Jeanne d'Arc.
new.tip: Allow one to two hours. Entry to the nave is free; check opening times for the towers.
new.q: Cathédrale Sainte-Croix, Place Sainte-Croix, Orléans

new.title: Meet Joan of Arc at the Maison de Jeanne d'Arc
new.desc: A reconstruction of the house where Joan of Arc stayed in 1429 during the siege of Orléans. The original was destroyed in the Second World War and the house was rebuilt in 1965; it now holds a museum on her story.
new.tip: Free on the first Sunday of the month and for under-26s; confirm hours on the museum site before going.
new.q: Maison de Jeanne d'Arc, 3 Place du Général de Gaulle, Orléans

new.title: Step inside the Renaissance Hôtel Groslot
new.desc: Built between 1530 and 1550 for the bailiff Jacques Groslot, this mansion became the town hall in 1790. The young king François II stayed here in 1560 and died in the house that December.
new.tip: It stands on Place de l'Étape next to the cathedral; interiors open at set times, so ask at the tourist office opposite.
new.q: Hôtel Groslot, Place de l'Étape, Orléans

new.title: See pastels at the Musée des Beaux-Arts d'Orléans
new.desc: Founded in 1797, this is one of France's oldest provincial museums, with European painting, sculpture and drawings from the 15th to the 20th century. Its pastel collection is said to be the second largest in France after the Louvre.
new.tip: A combined ticket with the archaeology museum has been offered; Friday evenings run late.
new.q: Musée des Beaux-Arts, 1 Rue Fernand Rabier, Orléans

new.title: Salute Joan of Arc's statue on Place du Martroi
new.desc: The bronze equestrian statue by Denis Foyatier was inaugurated in 1855 on the main square of Orléans. The square is lined with shops and cafés and is the centre of the Fêtes de Jeanne d'Arc.
new.tip: Best in the evening when the terraces fill; the tram stops here.
new.q: Place du Martroi, Orléans

new.title: Stroll the arcades of the Campo Santo
new.desc: Orléans' former grand cemetery is a rectangular garden framed by 16th-century arcaded galleries. It was first used as a burial ground in the 12th century and now hosts contemporary art shows.
new.tip: Check the tourist office for exhibitions and concerts held in the galleries.
new.q: Campo Santo, Rue Dupanloup, Orléans

new.title: Find the Neuvy-en-Sullias bronze horse at Hôtel Cabu
new.desc: This Renaissance mansion, built around 1550 for Philippe Cabu and bought by the city in 1862, holds the history and archaeology museum. Its star is the Gallo-Roman treasure of Neuvy-en-Sullias found in 1861, including a 1.12 m bronze horse.
new.tip: Tickets were listed at 6 euros full price; confirm opening days locally.
new.q: Hôtel Cabu, Square Abbé Desnoyers, Orléans

new.title: Explore natural history at the MOBE museum
new.desc: The Muséum d'Orléans pour la Biodiversité et l'Environnement reopened in 2021 after six years of renovation. Five levels cover invertebrates, birds, mammals, geology and Loire Valley prehistory.
new.tip: Free on the first Sunday of the month; opens at noon on some weekdays.
new.q: Muséum d'Orléans (MOBE), 6 Rue Marcel Proust, Orléans

new.title: Visit radical architecture at FRAC Les Turbulences
new.desc: The Frac Centre-Val de Loire moved in 2013 to a building by Jakob+MacFarlane on the former military supply depot. Its collection covers experimental art and architecture from 1950 to today.
new.tip: Open Wednesday to Sunday afternoons with free entry according to recent listings.
new.q: Les Turbulences - Frac Centre, 88 Rue du Colombier, Orléans

new.title: Find the Loiret's spring in the Parc Floral de la Source
new.desc: A 35-hectare garden park, labelled Jardin remarquable, where the Loiret river wells up at the Bouillon spring. It has flower beds, a butterfly house, a rose and Japanese garden and a small train.
new.tip: Closed 25 December and 1 January; hours and prices change with the season.
new.q: Parc Floral de la Source, Avenue du Parc Floral, Orléans

new.title: Wander the 1834 greenhouses of the Jardin des Plantes
new.desc: The botanical garden of about 3.5 hectares moved to the left bank of the Loire in 1834. Its old greenhouses shelter ferns, orchids and carnivorous plants, and an international rose contest has run here since 1958.
new.tip: Rose season peaks around September.
new.q: Jardin des Plantes, Orléans

new.title: Smell Renaissance perfumes at Château de Chamerolles
new.desc: Lancelot du Lac built this château between 1500 and 1530 for Louis XII's circle. Since 1992 it houses a museum on perfume and hygiene, set in about 5 hectares of gardens.
new.tip: Closed 25 December and in January; confirm hours before the drive.
new.q: Château de Chamerolles, Chilleurs-aux-Bois

new.title: Tour the bishops' château in Meung-sur-Loire
new.desc: The château was the residence of the bishops of Orléans until the Revolution. The visit covers more than 20 furnished rooms, attics and underground passages.
new.tip: Guided tours run through the day; a Christmas visit was planned for December 2026.
new.q: Château de Meung-sur-Loire, 16 Place du Martroi, Meung-sur-Loire

new.title: Cross Beaugency's medieval bridge to the Tour de l'Horloge
new.desc: The Tour de l'Horloge, also called Tour du Change, is a remnant of the town's second wall and still houses the municipal clock. The 460 m bridge over the Loire, with 24 spans, is first mentioned in 1145.
new.tip: Walk the old town and the bridge together; the tower opens for occasional visits.
new.q: Tour de l'Horloge (Tour du Change), Rue du Change, Beaugency

new.title: Explore Château de Sully-sur-Loire
new.desc: A medieval fortress on the Loire with Renaissance interiors, home of the Duke of Sully. The Sully family kept it until the 20th century, and the Loiret département now owns and restores it.
new.tip: Summer hours run daily; winter opening is limited.
new.q: Château de Sully-sur-Loire, Sully-sur-Loire

new.title: See the Carolingian mosaic at Germigny-des-Prés
new.desc: Bishop Theodulf built this oratory between 803 and 806. Its apse mosaic of two angels and the Ark of the Covenant dates from the 9th century.
new.tip: Guided visits and night openings are offered; check the tourist office.
new.q: Oratoire carolingien de Germigny-des-Prés, Germigny-des-Prés

new.title: Descend to the crypt at Saint-Benoît-sur-Loire Abbey
new.desc: The Romanesque basilica of Fleury Abbey keeps the relics of Saint Benedict in its 11th-century crypt. It is still a working monastery with monks chanting the services.
new.tip: Worship has priority over tourism; from winter to Easter services move to the crypt.
new.q: Abbaye de Fleury, Saint-Benoît-sur-Loire

new.title: Visit the hunting museum in Gien's château
new.desc: The brick-and-stone château was built at the end of the 15th century for Anne de Beaujeu. It houses a hunting museum opened in 1952, later refocused on hunting, history and nature in the Loire.
new.tip: Reopened in April 2024 after works; check current prices.
new.q: Château de Gien, Place Anne de Beaujeu, Gien

new.title: Cross the Anne-de-Beaujeu bridge for the Gien skyline
new.desc: The current bridge dates from 1734 after a flood took three arches in 1733. It frames the town and its château, beside the church rebuilt in 1954 after the 1940 bombings.
new.tip: Best light at sunset from the quay.
new.q: Vieux pont de Gien, Gien

new.title: Browse the Faïencerie de Gien museum
new.desc: The museum opened in 1985 in the former Minimes convent to show pieces kept since the factory's creation in 1821. The factory shop sells tableware on the same site.
new.tip: Guided tours last about 60 minutes; adults paid 8 euros per the official site.
new.q: Faïencerie de Gien, Place de la Victoire, Gien

new.title: Walk the Briare canal bridge over the Loire
new.desc: This 662 m aqueduct built by Eiffel's firm carries the Canal latéral à la Loire on fourteen piers. It is the longest canal aqueduct in France and is lit at night.
new.tip: It sits on the Loire à Vélo route; walk across the towpath.
new.q: Pont-canal de Briare, Briare

new.title: See Girodet's paintings in Montargis
new.desc: The Musée Girodet is housed in the Hôtel Durzy and focuses on Anne-Louis Girodet-Trioson, born in Montargis in 1767. It also shows works by Géricault and others.
new.tip: Check musee-girodet.fr for hours.
new.q: Musée Girodet, 2 Rue du Faubourg de la Chaussée, Montargis

new.title: Visit the abbey of Ferrières-en-Gâtinais
new.desc: This former Benedictine abbey of Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul is a Petite Cité de Caractère. The listed Notre-Dame de Bethléem chapel dates from the 15th century and a pilgrimage is held in early September.
new.tip: Combine with a walk in the village.
new.q: Ancienne abbaye, Ferrières-en-Gâtinais

new.title: Discover the fishing museum at Château de la Bussière
new.desc: A brick château on a six-hectare pond in a park attributed to Le Nôtre, known as the Château des Pêcheurs. It holds freshwater fishing art within family furnishings and is a listed monument.
new.tip: Opening days vary; confirm on the château site.
new.q: Château de la Bussière, La Bussière

new.title: Pay respects to Louis XI at Cléry-Saint-André
new.desc: The basilica became a royal chapel under Louis XI, who chose it as burial place. His kneeling bronze effigy and his tomb lie inside; Leo XIII made it a basilica in 1894.
new.tip: Combine with the Loire à Vélo ride from Orléans.
new.q: Basilique Notre-Dame de Cléry, Cléry-Saint-André

new.title: Learn Loire boatman lore at the Musée de la Marine de Loire
new.desc: Set in the 17th-century stables of Châteauneuf's château, the museum covers navigation on the Loire over three levels and the town's metal-bridge industry.
new.tip: Closed Tuesdays and on three public holidays.
new.q: Musée de la Marine de Loire, 1 Place Aristide Briand, Châteauneuf-sur-Loire

new.title: Walk among 2,600 species at the Arboretum des Barres
new.desc: A 35-hectare national arboretum within a forest of nearly 300 hectares, with over 2,500 species and the Jardin remarquable label since 2004.
new.tip: Open daily in warmer months with an admission fee; a nursery sells rare plants.
new.q: Arboretum national des Barres, Nogent-sur-Vernisson

new.title: Follow Joan of Arc's 1429 victory along Jargeau's Loire
new.desc: Joan of Arc won the battle of Jargeau on 12 June 1429, a key step in clearing the Loire of the English. The riverside has promenades and a bridge to Mardié.
new.tip: Swimming in the Loire is not allowed here.
new.q: Porte Madeleine and Loire quays, Jargeau

new.title: Learn about Gâtinais saffron at the Boynes saffron museum
new.desc: Five rooms cover the red gold of the Gâtinais, its history and saffron production, which was first cultivated in Boynes. The museum opened in 1997.
new.tip: Phone ahead (02 38 33 13 05) to confirm hours.
new.q: Musée du Safran, 21 Route de Pithiviers, Boynes

new.title: Sip a drink at Le Ponton guinguette on the Loire
new.desc: Le Ponton, successor to La Sardine, is the guinguette on the quai du Châtelet with local organic products and a cultural programme. The city guinguette guide for 2026 lists it.
new.tip: Summer season; confirm opening on leponton-orleans.fr.
new.q: Le Ponton, Quai du Châtelet, Orléans

new.title: Shop cheese and fish at Les Halles Châtelet
new.desc: The covered food market has stalls of cheesemongers, a baker and fishmongers such as Poissonnerie Royale. The city is preparing a food-focused redevelopment.
new.tip: Check which stalls are open during the redevelopment.
new.q: Les Halles Châtelet, Place du Châtelet, Orléans

new.title: Share natural-wine plates at Les Becs à Vin
new.desc: A natural-wine bar, bistro and shop at Place du Châtelet with over 200 organic and biodynamic references and small daily plates around 9 to 16 euros.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Saturday evenings; book ahead.
new.q: Les Becs à Vin, 8 Place du Châtelet, Orléans

new.title: Dine at Le Lièvre Gourmand on the quai
new.desc: Chef Tristan Robreau runs this Gault&Millau Table Remarquable at 28 quai du Châtelet, rated 15/20 in the 2026 guide, with menus at about 82 to 116 euros.
new.tip: Book ahead.
new.q: Le Lièvre Gourmand, 28 Quai du Châtelet, Orléans

new.title: Buy pralinés at the Chocolaterie Royale
new.desc: A well-regarded chocolatier on rue Royale known for its pralinés and truffles.
new.tip: Rue Royale links Place du Martroi and the Loire bridge.
new.q: Chocolaterie Royale, 51 Rue Royale, Orléans

new.title: Taste Orléans vinegar at La Boutique Martin Pouret
new.desc: Martin-Pouret has made Orléans vinegar since 1797 using the traditional method. Its boutique sells the vinegars and the tourist office has run guided factory visits with tastings.
new.tip: Tours need booking via the tourist office.
new.q: La Boutique Martin Pouret, 11 Rue Jeanne d'Arc, Orléans

new.title: Pair wine and plates at GlouGlou on rue de Bourgogne
new.desc: A restaurant, wine bar and terrace opened in 2023 at 157 rue de Bourgogne by a team passionate about wine and gastronomy.
new.tip: Terrace seats fill on summer evenings.
new.q: GlouGlou, 157 Rue de Bourgogne, Orléans

new.title: Taste cotignac d'Orléans from Maison Gouchault
new.desc: Cotignac is a quince paste-jelly confection of Orléans. Benoît Gouchault, in Saint-Ay since 1975, long made it and his nephew has revived the house, sold in partner shops in Orléans.
new.tip: Find it in Orléans partner shops or via the maker.
new.q: Benoît Gouchault Confiseur, 30 bis Rue de Voisinas, Saint-Ay

new.title: Buy pralines at the Maison de la Prasline Mazet
new.desc: Mazet has made Montargis pralines since Léon Mazet bought the recipe in 1903. The shop sells them loose from a large bowl in a neo-Gothic building.
new.tip: Opening hours unconfirmed; check mazetconfiseur.com.
new.q: Maison de la Prasline Mazet, 43 Rue du Général Leclerc, Montargis

new.title: Taste the Pithiviers at À la Renommée
new.desc: Stéphane Maréchal has run this pâtisserie since 1994 with an unchanged recipe, grinding whole blanched almonds in-house for his Pithiviers and little pomponettes.
new.tip: Ask for the fondant or feuilleté version.
new.q: À la Renommée, 5 Mail Ouest, Pithiviers

new.title: Dine on the terrace at Le P'tit Bateau in Beaugency
new.desc: A modern-cuisine restaurant at 54 rue du Pont with a shaded terrace and winter garden, near the Loire bridge.
new.tip: Book for summer evenings.
new.q: Le P'tit Bateau, 54 Rue du Pont, Beaugency

new.title: Eat a bistro lunch at Chez Henri II in Beaugency
new.desc: Traditional meals, salads and bistro dishes built on seasonal products, on rue du Pont with a terrace beside a small stream.
new.tip: Terrace is pleasant on dry days.
new.q: Chez Henri II, 43 Rue du Pont, Beaugency

new.title: Splurge at the Auberge des Templiers in Les Bézards
new.desc: A Relais & Châteaux inn since 1954 on the old Route Nationale, with a one-star Michelin table, modern cuisine and a menu around 139 euros in late 2025.
new.tip: Closed Tuesday and Wednesday; book well ahead.
new.q: Auberge des Templiers, 20 Route Départementale 2007, Les Bézards, Boismorand

new.title: Taste the Loire at La Table in Ardon
new.desc: Christophe Hay and Loïs Bée run this Gault&Millau Remarkable Restaurant, rated 16.5/20, at 200 Allée des Quatre Vents. Bée won the Grand de Demain 2026 award.
new.tip: Book far ahead.
new.q: La Table - Christophe Hay et Loïs Bée, 200 Allée des Quatre Vents, Ardon

new.title: Eat traditional French at Le P'tit Bouchon in Gien
new.desc: The only Gien address listed by Gault&Millau, rated 11/20, serving traditional cuisine from about 17.50 to 30 euros.
new.tip: Good for a lunch after the faience visit.
new.q: Le P'tit Bouchon, Gien

new.title: Lunch at Le Petit Saint-Trop by the Loire in Briare
new.desc: Gault&Millau lists this Briare restaurant, rated 11/20, whose review evokes the South from the banks of the Loire.
new.tip: Near the canal bridge.
new.q: Le Petit Saint-Trop, Briare

new.title: Try Olivet pear dishes at the Hostellerie du Grand Sully
new.desc: A hotel-restaurant in Sully-sur-Loire with chef Yves Dessaint, rated 11/20, whose 37 euro menu features Olivet pear.
new.tip: Walk to the château afterward.
new.q: Hostellerie du Grand Sully, Sully-sur-Loire

new.title: Eat traditional cuisine at Aux P'tits Augnons in Sully
new.desc: A traditional restaurant in the historic sailors' district of Sully-sur-Loire.
new.tip: Close to the château.
new.q: Aux P'tits Augnons, 1 Rue du Port au Bois, Sully-sur-Loire

new.title: Join the Fêtes de Jeanne d'Arc in Orléans
new.desc: Held every year from 29 April to 8 May to mark the lifting of the 1429 siege. The 8 May military parade and a commemorative procession led by Joan of Arc and her escort close the festivities.
new.tip: The 2026 edition ran 29 April to 10 May.
new.q: Place du Martroi, Orléans

new.title: See traditional boats at the Festival de Loire
new.desc: A biennial gathering of river craft on the Orléans quays in late September; the 12th edition ran 24 to 28 September 2025.
new.tip: Next edition expected September 2027, unconfirmed.
new.q: Quai du Châtelet, Orléans

new.title: Cruise the Loire in a traditional boat from Orléans
new.desc: A 30-minute trip on a traditional boat costs about 8.50 euros per adult; a one-hour trip is 15 euros. July to September boats leave beside Le Ponton.
new.tip: Reserve the one-hour trip.
new.q: Place du Châtelet, Orléans

new.title: Bar-hop along rue de Bourgogne
new.desc: Nearly 600 m long between Place du Martroi and rue Royale, the street is the busiest after 8pm with bars, restaurants and terraces such as Le Orléans and Mc Ewan's Café.
new.tip: Go on a warm evening for the terraces.
new.q: Rue de Bourgogne, Orléans

new.title: Walk the banks of the Loiret in Olivet
new.desc: Marked trails follow the Loiret river banks from the Parc du Poutyl, a French-style garden with a terrace overlooking the river.
new.tip: Access to the river paths and Poutyl is free.
new.q: Parc du Poutyl, Olivet

new.title: Cycle the Loire à Vélo from Orléans to Beaugency
new.desc: The Orléans to Beaugency stage is about 29 km, shared with EuroVelo 6, via Meung-sur-Loire, mixing dedicated paths and quiet roads.
new.tip: Cross the Meung bridge with care.
new.q: Quai du Châtelet, Orléans

new.title: Ride the Briare to Gien stretch of Loire à Vélo
new.desc: A 12 km stage over small country roads from the Briare canal bridge toward Gien, known for its pottery.
new.tip: Trains from Paris carry bikes.
new.q: Pont-canal de Briare, Briare

new.title: Cycle Sully-sur-Loire to Briare
new.desc: The Scandibérique and Loire à Vélo route links the château of Sully to Briare along the river and canal.
new.tip: Plan a stop at Gien on the way.
new.q: Château de Sully-sur-Loire, Sully-sur-Loire

new.title: Ride the old canal towpath near Châtillon-sur-Loire
new.desc: A 4.3 km gravel green way follows the old Loire lateral canal towpath to Port des Combles, before the Châtillon-sur-Loire bridge.
new.tip: Mantelot lock is worth a look.
new.q: Ancien canal latéral à la Loire, Port des Combles, Châtillon-sur-Loire

new.title: Hike round the Étang de la Vallée in the Forêt d'Orléans
new.desc: A 7 to 11 km loop from the leisure base car park passes the Caillettes viewpoint, 126 steps high with canopy views. The pond was dug to feed the Canal d'Orléans.
new.tip: Forest tracks beyond are restricted to rights holders.
new.q: Base de loisirs de l'étang de la Vallée, Combreux

new.title: Hike the Sologne forest from Ligny-le-Ribault
new.desc: A loop from the church square follows wide forest tracks through La Bretèche and La Couvrée to the ecomuseum; the Circuit de la Couvré is 15.4 km.
new.tip: Many areas are private; stay on waymarked paths.
new.q: Place de l'église, Ligny-le-Ribault

new.title: Cruise the canals of Montargis, Venice of the Gâtinais
new.desc: The Loing and the Briare canal encircle the town, and a commented boat cruise is the best way to see its bridges. The agglomeration's boat Zia carried over 3,000 passengers in its first ten weeks in 2025.
new.tip: Check the tourist office for the season schedule.
new.q: Quai Baudin, Montargis

new.title: Taste AOC Orléans wines at Clos Saint-Fiacre
new.desc: A family estate in Mareau-aux-Prés, vines grown since the 17th century, producing AOC Orléans and Orléans-Cléry.
new.tip: Tastings by appointment, Monday to Saturday.
new.q: Clos Saint-Fiacre, 560 Rue Saint-Fiacre, Mareau-aux-Prés

new.title: Hear Gregorian chant at Fleury Abbey
new.desc: The monks chant prayers six times a day in Gregorian monophony; Sunday mass is at 11am and weekday mass at noon according to older listings.
new.tip: Check current times on abbaye-fleury.com.
new.q: Abbaye de Fleury, Saint-Benoît-sur-Loire

new.title: Tour the Faïencerie de Gien workshops
new.desc: Seasonal guided workshop tours show the main stages of faience manufacture; one 2025 listing priced it at 18 euros.
new.tip: Book ahead.
new.q: Faïencerie de Gien, Place de la Victoire, Gien

new.title: Ride the tourist train at the Pithiviers transport museum
new.desc: The Musée des Transports on rue Carnot has kept historic equipment running since 1966 and runs a tourist railway.
new.tip: Check seasonal running days.
new.q: Musée des Transports, Rue Carnot, Pithiviers
